Fit the Equation (6) Model by Maximum Likelihood

Source: R/GGcov_MLE.R
GGcov_MLE.Rd

Fits the model in which, for each subject, the outcomes z_1, ..., z_x are gamma distributed with shape p and rate nu0 * exp(-w_i beta'), and nu0 has a gamma(q, gamma) distribution that is integrated out (equation 6). Covariates are centered and scaled internally for numerical stability, and the results are converted back to the original covariate scale.

Usage

GGcov_MLE(fo, data, subject, level = 0.95)

Arguments

fo

Formula z ~ w1 + w2 + ...: the outcome on the left, plain covariate names on the right. Transformations such as log(x) or I(x^2) and interactions are rejected with an error; create transformed variables as new columns in data first. Do not include an intercept: gamma plays that role. Use z ~ 1 to fit the null model with no covariates (p, q and gamma only); it is nested in any model with covariates (all coefficients equal to 0), so 2 * (null$value - full$value) is a likelihood-ratio statistic with one degree of freedom per coefficient.

data

Data frame in long format, one row per subject per period. Row order does not matter. Covariates may be time-varying or static: a static covariate is handled by repeating its value on each of the subject's rows.

subject

Character string naming the subject ID column in data.

level

Confidence level for the Wald intervals, strictly between 0 and 1. Default 0.95.

Value

A list of class "GGcov" containing the optim results with additional elements. All estimates, standard errors and bounds are on the original covariate scale (only hessian is on the internal parameterization):

par

Estimates: p (shape), q (mixture shape: the shape of the gamma mixing distribution of nu0), gamma (mixture rate: its rate), then the covariate coefficients.

par_stderr

Standard errors. For p, q and gamma these use the delta method, e.g. SE(p) is approximately p * SE(log p). NA with a warning if the Hessian is not positive definite.

par_lower, par_upper

Wald limits at level. For p, q and gamma the interval is built on the log scale and exponentiated.

level

The confidence level used.

value

Negative log-likelihood at the optimum.

convergence

optim convergence code (0 = success; any other code triggers a warning).

hessian

Hessian on the internal parameterization (log p, log q, log gamma, standardized coefficients).

center, scale

Covariate means and standard deviations used internally.

terms, xlevels

Covariate terms and factor levels, for coding new data.

spend_name, subject_name

Names of the outcome and subject columns used in the fit, so GGcov_expected_spend can find them in new data.

Examples

fit <- GGcov_MLE(
  Price ~ discount + gender + channel,
  data    = spend_data_sample,
  subject = "Id"
)
print(fit)
#> Gamma-gamma model 
#> 
#>                      Estimate Std. Error Lower 95% Upper 95%
#> p (shape)              1.9180    0.09844    1.7350    2.1210
#> q (mixture shape)      9.6130    2.20000    6.1390   15.0500
#> gamma (mixture rate) 238.6000   66.28000  138.5000  411.3000
#> discount              -0.6560    0.17840   -1.0060   -0.3064
#> gendermale            -0.2609    0.06924   -0.3967   -0.1252
#> channelweb             0.3511    0.08093    0.1924    0.5097
#> channelapp            -0.3867    0.08946   -0.5621   -0.2114
#> 
#> Negative log-likelihood: 3981.2844
#> Convergence code: 0

# Null model without covariates
fit_null <- GGcov_MLE(Price ~ 1, data = spend_data_sample, subject = "Id")
print(fit_null)
#> Gamma-gamma model 
#> 
#>                      Estimate Std. Error Lower 95% Upper 95%
#> p (shape)               1.901    0.09849     1.717     2.104
#> q (mixture shape)       5.631    0.95590     4.037     7.853
#> gamma (mixture rate)  106.000   22.53000    69.920   160.800
#> 
#> Negative log-likelihood: 4017.5628
#> Convergence code: 0
